## Overview

`rejection_sample` accepts a precomputed fp64 `target_lse`, and `RejectionSampler` passes the one `topp_cutoffs_lse` (#65101) already computes alongside the cutoffs, so on the top-p-on-load path (#65102) the stats kernel no longer reduces the target logits a second time. 4/4 of a stack; part of #61024.

**Stacked, draft.** Contains #65101 and #65102 (with #61344's commits), then the commit of #64242 (by AlejandroParedesLT, authorship kept), which fixes the near-1 collapse of the global log-sum-exp by promoting it to fp64. **New code is five commits:** the target log-sum-exp from the cutoff op; #64242's per-element math in fp32 (co-authored with AlejandroParedesLT); dropping the op's log-sum-exp when verification narrows the vocab; the global combine itself in fp32 with #64242's precision; and, last, keeping the max's 1 out of the block sums and the resample residual nonzero, from #65176 (co-authored with shiannn13). The two commits before the last are #65101's kernel rework, cherry-picked. After those come the 2026-11-03 fixes carried from #65101 and #65102: #65101's int64 index-mapping fix, #65100's commit with its block skip firing on the on-load path, and #65102's end-to-end `LLM` test.

**Fix (2026-11-03).** The first top-p request took EngineCore down: `topp_cutoffs_lse` accepted only an int32 `expanded_idx_mapping`, while Model Runner V2 builds int64 index mappings (#60736). Fixed in #65101 and carried here with the rest of #65102's fixes (details there).

## Claims

- Verification step for top-p requests (K = 3, top-p 0.95, Qwen3-0.6B creative-writing logits, GB300), after #65102: 457 → 400 µs at 256 requests with T = 1 and 485 → 410 µs with T = 0.7 (vLLM main: 2,122 and 2,158 µs).
- MiniMax-M3.1-like verification (DSpark K = 7, block verification, V = 200,064, top-p 0.95): **2.8–5.3× faster than main at T = 0.95** from 1 to 128 requests, 2.9–5.5× at T = 1.
- With #65100's resample skip firing on the on-load path (from #65102), `rejection_sample` with the op's cutoffs and log-sum-exp (real Qwen3-0.6B rows, K = 3, top-p 0.95, T = 1) goes **262 → 138 µs** at 256 requests, 72 → 42 µs at 64 and 29 → 22 µs at 16, bitwise identical. The step times below predate it.
- **#64242's fix without its fp64 cost.** As written, its fp64 math made block verification 2–4× slower than main on GB300 (low fp64 throughput; the combine runs in every program of the per-block kernels). Here the combine is fp32 and as precise: each block's sum leaves out its own max and the combine adds the other blocks' 1 back, so the max token's 1 is never added; `log1p` of the rest keeps a runner-up far below the max, and the result is an exact `hi + lo` pair that `x - lse` consumes as `(x - hi) - lo`. #64242's own test passes (its probe's block sums follow that convention); on 65K synthetic partial sets the log-sum-exp is within 5.5×10⁻⁷ of fp64 (the fp64 combine: 5.2×10⁻⁷; both set by the fp32 block sums).
- **Resampling stays in the target's support** (#61383; fixes and test from #65176 by shiannn13). When the draft puts all but e^-gap of its mass on the one token the target allows, two fp32 roundings emptied the residual and the resample emitted token 0: `1 + e^-gap` inside an 8,192-token block, and `exp(log q - log p)` rounding to 1 in the residual. Block sums now leave one max element out, and the residual is `log p + log(1 - exp(log q - log p))` with the existing series for `1 - exp` near 0 (no libdevice). The previous head resamples token 0 at gap 25; this keeps the allowed token. Cost: +4% of the step at 256 requests (K = 3), +2–4% elsewhere, by counting the max's ties instead of taking its index (an argmax per block cost +20%).
- Never slower than main across a 360-configuration stress matrix (1.04–8.3×, median 3.6×, run with #65101's first commit), and within 4% of #65102 at the median; the largest remaining gap is +3.7 µs (+13%) at 1 request, K = 7, block verification, top-p = 1, where no op log-sum-exp is available and the combine runs serially per position.
- Same samples as the stats pass's own log-sum-exp (test below). The value is over the same `x / T` (rounded to nearest) the verify kernels use, so the max token's log-probability is never positive: with top-p = 1 on 2,048 real rows, vLLM main's fp32 log-sum-exp leaves p_max at exactly 1.0 in 77 rows (T = 1), #64242 alone in none, this in none.

```
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
    tests/kernels/test_topp_cutoffs_lse.py -q
# 242 passed, 4 skipped (GB300), including #64242's test_global_logsumexp_keeps_near_max_correction

# 1 passed (GB300): Qwen3.5-0.8B + MTP serving temperature 1 / top-p 0.95 through the op
```

| T | requests | main µs | #65102 µs | this branch µs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 66.7 | 25.2 | 24.5 |
| 1 | 16 | 322.6 | 46.5 | 45.2 |
| 1 | 64 | 654.1 | 132.9 | 119.9 |
| 1 | 256 | 2,122.4 | 457.4 | 399.6 |
| 0.7 | 1 | 68.5 | 26.3 | 25.1 |
| 0.7 | 16 | 330.2 | 49.3 | 46.9 |
| 0.7 | 256 | 2,158.0 | 485.4 | 409.6 |

| requests | 1 | 4 | 16 | 64 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T = 0.95 | 2.81× | 4.28× | 5.27× | 5.23× | 5.12× |
| T = 1 | 2.85× | 4.34× | 5.47× | 5.25× | 5.13× |

<summary>Stress test (harness not part of this PR) and what it changed here</summary>

- A target vocab wider than the draft's (padded lm_head, as with MiMo + DFlash): `rejection_sample` verifies over the draft vocab only, but the op's log-sum-exp covered the extra columns, so with padding the mask keeps, this branch agreed with #65102 on 0–33% of requests. - **How.** The op's log-sum-exp reaches every kernel that combines target partials as two fp32 partials per row (`-inf`/0 in the other blocks), so none of those kernels changes; the stats kernel skips its target pass under `HAS_TARGET_LSE`, and greedy rows still compute their block maxes for the argmax. Hi @zyongye, I've been working on #61383 too, and part of my change overlaps with yours. I opened #65176 as a draft to share it.

Like this PR, it carries the log-sum-exp as a (max, correction) pair and computes (x - max) - correction. That part overlaps with your (hi, lo) approach, so there's no need to duplicate it. It also does two things that #61383's failing state still needs.

**Per-block sumexp without the max's 1:**
I noticed that the latest commit subtracts the max token's contribution of 1 during the global merge. However, when the max and runner-up share an 8,192-token block, `1 + exp(-18)` already rounds to `1.0` in the per-block stats pass, so subtracting 1 during the merge cannot recover the lost correction.

In #65176, the stats kernel instead excludes one max element from each block's sum to avoid this precision loss. In #61383, this issue occurs on the draft side, where `q(") ≈ 1 - exp(-gap)` and there's no op-provided log-sum-exp.

**expm1 residual:** 
_resample_kernel computes log_p + log(-expm1(log_q - log_p)) instead of log1p(-exp(delta)). With delta ≈ -1.5e-8, exp(delta) rounds to exactly 1.0, so the residual is empty even when both log-sum-exps are exact.
On a reconstruction of the issue's state (real XGrammar + Qwen3-4B tokenizer, top-k/top-p, a draft that isn't grammar-masked), main and #64242 both still emit token 0 at gap ≥ 18.

I also ran the test on this branch (ae6817425a, RTX 2050), with the test added unchanged to test_rejection_sampler_utils.py. Gaps 10 and 14 pass, but gap 25 fails under both standard and block verification: assert [1, 2, 0] == [1, 2, 3], i.e. it still resamples token 0. The other 134 tests in that file pass.

If #65103 lands first, I'm happy to rebase #65176 onto it as a follow-up with just the per-block sumexp, the expm1 residual and the test. If you'd rather fold those into your stack instead, that works for me too.

Thanks @shiannn13, you're right on both counts. The `(hi, lo)` combine here only dropped the max's 1 after each 8,192-token block had already rounded `1 + e^-gap` to 1, and the residual still went through `exp(log_q - log_p)`.

I folded both fixes and your test into this PR as e7251a11e3, with you as co-author (`Co-authored-by: Andy Shih <shiannn@icloud.com>`). Two changes from #65176:

- **Ties counted instead of an index.** The block sum leaves out one max element by counting the max's ties (`sum over x != max` plus `ties - 1`), not by taking its index. On GB300 the per-block argmax cost +20% of the verification step (K = 3, 256 requests). The tie count costs +4%, and +2–4% elsewhere.
- **Series instead of `expm1`.** The residual uses the file's existing `1 - exp(x)` series near 0 instead of libdevice `expm1`. That removes libdevice from the resample kernel and is slightly faster.

`test_resample_stays_in_target_support` is unchanged. On the previous head (78b066a8c1) it fails at gap 25 for both standard and block verification (`[1, 2, 0] == [1, 2, 3]`), as you found; it passes now along with the rest of the suite (234 passed on GB300). #64242's probe test now feeds block sums in the new convention.

Since the `(max, correction)` pair is already here, this should cover #65176 completely. Feel free to close it, or keep it open as the fallback if this stack stalls.

merged. Please rebase the PR, @zyongye.

+"""Benchmark topp_cutoffs_lse against the top-p path it replaces in verification.
+
+The baseline is what MRV2's rejection sampler runs today for top-p requests:
+an fp32 copy of the bf16 target logits, the temperature kernel and the Triton
+top-k/top-p mask. topp_cutoffs_lse reads the bf16 logits once and writes one
+cutoff and one log-sum-exp per row; "op" lets it pick the cluster size, "C=4"
+forces four CTAs per row. --force-fallback times the precise (1) or fp64 (2)
+path on every row.
+
+    .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_topp_cutoffs_lse.py
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import statistics
+from functools import partial
+
+import torch
+from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+from vllm.v1.sample.ops.topk_topp_sampler import apply_top_k_top_p
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.gumbel import apply_temperature
+
+
+def bench_us(fn) -> float:
+    for _ in range(10):
+        fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn)) * 1e3

+        f"{'vocab':>7} {'rows':>5} {'baseline us':>12} {'C=4 us':>8} {'op us':>8} "
+        f"{'op GB/s':>8}"
+    )
+    for vocab in args.vocab:
+        for rows in args.rows:
+            # A Gaussian body under a few dominant tokens, like LM logits. Flat
+            # rows (large-sigma Gaussians) sometimes take the fp64 path instead.
+            logits = torch.randn(rows, vocab, device="cuda") * 2
+            spikes = torch.randint(0, vocab, (rows, 4), device="cuda")
+            logits.scatter_(1, spikes, 12 + torch.rand(rows, 4, device="cuda") * 6)
+            logits = logits.to(torch.bfloat16)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""topp_cutoffs_lse against an fp64 reference over x / T.
+
+The op keeps every token tied with the cutoff, so the reference sorts the row
+and keeps every value at or above the first one whose cumulative probability
+reaches top_p. The op picks how many CTAs share a row from the batch size;
+the tests also force each cluster size, since each takes its own path.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not (
+    current_platform.is_cuda()
+    and current_platform.has_device_capability(90)
+    and ops.has_topp_cutoffs_lse()
+):
+    pytest.skip("topp_cutoffs_lse requires SM90+", allow_module_level=True)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+
+
+def _params(num_rows: int, temperature: float, top_p: float):
+    idx = torch.arange(num_rows, dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE)
+    temp = torch.full((num_rows,), temperature, device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.full((num_rows,), top_p, device=DEVICE)
+    return idx, temp, p
+
+
+def _reference(
+    logits: torch.Tensor, temp: torch.Tensor, top_p: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """fp64 ties-kept cutoff and kept log-sum-exp over x / T (fp32, IEEE)."""
+    x = logits.float()
+    scaled = x / temp[:, None]
+    order = x.argsort(dim=-1, descending=True)
+    sorted_x = x.gather(1, order)
+    probs = torch.softmax(scaled.gather(1, order).double(), dim=-1)
+    reach = (probs.cumsum(-1) < top_p.double()[:, None]).sum(-1)
+    cut = sorted_x.gather(1, reach.clamp(max=x.shape[1] - 1)[:, None])[:, 0]
+    cut = torch.where(top_p >= 1, float("-inf"), cut)
+    kept = torch.where(x >= cut[:, None], scaled.double(), float("-inf"))
+    return cut, kept.logsumexp(-1)
+
+
+def _logits(num_rows: int, vocab_size: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """bf16 rows with a few dominant tokens over a Gaussian body; bf16 rounding
+    makes ties at every value."""
+    x = torch.randn(num_rows, vocab_size, device=DEVICE) * 2
+    spikes = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (num_rows, 4), device=DEVICE)
+    x.scatter_(1, spikes, 12 + torch.rand(num_rows, 4, device=DEVICE) * 6)
+    return x.to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("vocab_size", [32000, 151936, 262144])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("temperature", [0.7, 1.0])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_p", [0.5, 0.95])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cluster_size", [0, 1, 2, 4])
+def test_matches_fp64_reference(
+    vocab_size: int, temperature: float, top_p: float, cluster_size: int
+):
+    if cluster_size == 4 and vocab_size > 4 * 65528:
+        pytest.skip("a CTA slice of 4 would overflow its u16 counts")
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    logits = _logits(64, vocab_size)
+    idx, temp, p = _params(64, temperature, top_p)
+
+    thresh, lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p, cluster_size)
+    ref_thresh, ref_lse = _reference(logits, temp, p)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(thresh, ref_thresh, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lse, ref_lse, rtol=0, atol=1e-6)
+    # The max token's log-probability x~max - lse is never positive.
+    scaled_max = (logits.float() / temp[:, None]).max(-1).values.double()
+    assert (lse >= scaled_max).all()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cluster_size", [1, 4])
+def test_fallback_paths_match_integer_path(cluster_size: int):
+    """Rows the integer search cannot settle are redone by the precise
+    fixed-point path, then by fp64; forcing either on every row must give the
+    same cutoffs."""
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    logits = _logits(32, 151936)
+    idx, temp, p = _params(32, 0.7, 0.9)
+
+    thresh, lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p, cluster_size)
+    for force in (1, 2):
+        thresh_f, lse_f = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(
+            logits, idx, temp, p, cluster_size, force_fallback=force
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(thresh_f, thresh, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(lse_f, lse, rtol=0, atol=1e-6)
+
+
+def test_precise_path_matches_fp64_path():
+    """Flat rows (bf16 Gaussians) put the cutoff among many near-equal masses,
+    where the integer search often defers; the precise path settles them like
+    fp64 does."""
+    torch.manual_seed(3)
+    logits = (torch.randn(64, 151936, device=DEVICE) * 3).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    idx, temp, p = _params(64, 1.0, 0.95)
+
+    precise = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p, force_fallback=1)
+    fp64 = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p, force_fallback=2)
+    ref_thresh, _ = _reference(logits, temp, p)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(precise[0], fp64[0], rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(precise[0], ref_thresh, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(precise[1], fp64[1], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cluster_size", [0, 1])
+def test_row_kinds(cluster_size: int):
+    vocab_size = 20000
+    logits = _logits(5, vocab_size)
+    logits[3] = float("-inf")  # no finite logit
+    logits[4, 7] = float("inf")
+    idx = torch.arange(5, dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE)
+    # Greedy, top_p = 1, top_p < 1, then the two special rows.
+    temp = torch.tensor([0.0, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0, 1.0], device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.tensor([0.9, 1.0, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9], device=DEVICE)
+
+    thresh, lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p, cluster_size)
+    ref_thresh, ref_lse = _reference(logits[1:3], temp[1:3], p[1:3])
+
+    assert thresh[0] == float("-inf") and torch.isnan(lse[0])
+    torch.testing.assert_close(thresh[1:3], ref_thresh, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lse[1:3], ref_lse, rtol=0, atol=1e-6)
+    assert thresh[3] == float("-inf") and lse[3] == float("-inf")
+    assert thresh[4] == float("inf") and lse[4] == float("inf")
+
+
+def test_runner_up_far_below_max():
+    """The kept mass beside the max token is resolved down to 2^-40 of it, so
+    the max token's probability stays below 1 for gaps up to 40 ln 2."""
+    gaps = [4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 27]
+    logits = torch.full((len(gaps), 151936), -40.0, device=DEVICE)
+    for i, g in enumerate(gaps):
+        logits[i, 1000] = 25.0
+        logits[i, 30000] = 25.0 - g
+    logits = logits.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    idx, temp, p = _params(len(gaps), 1.0, 1.0)
+
+    _, lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p)
+
+    expected = torch.tensor(
+        [math.log1p(math.exp(-g)) for g in gaps], dtype=torch.float64, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    # Each runner-up's fixed-point mass is floored to an integer of 2^-40 units.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lse - 25.0, expected, rtol=0.05, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_strided_rows_match_contiguous():
+    """A row stride of V + 3 also leaves odd rows off 16-byte alignment, which
+    takes the scalar-load path."""
+    torch.manual_seed(2)
+    padded = _logits(16, 151936 + 3)
+    logits = padded[:, :151936]
+    idx, temp, p = _params(16, 0.9, 0.95)
+
+    thresh, lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p)
+    ref_thresh, ref_lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits.contiguous(), idx, temp, p)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(thresh, ref_thresh, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lse, ref_lse, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cluster_size", [1, 2])
+def test_u16_count_wraps(cluster_size: int):
+    """A CTA slice over 65,535 tokens can push one key's u16 count past
+    0xFFFF; the op recounts such slices with every wrap recorded."""
+    torch.manual_seed(4)
+    vocab_size = 202048
+    logits = _logits(4, vocab_size)
+    lo = torch.tensor(1.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    hi = (lo.view(torch.int16) + 1).view(torch.bfloat16)  # the next key up
+    logits[0, :70000] = lo
+    logits[1, :70000] = lo  # the even key wraps and carries into the odd one
+    logits[1, 70000:140000] = hi
+    logits[2, :131072] = lo  # two wraps of one key
+    logits[3, ::2] = lo
+    idx, temp, p = _params(4, 1.0, 0.9)
+
+    thresh, lse = ops.topp_cutoffs_lse(logits, idx, temp, p, cluster_size)

+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(thresh, ref_thresh, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lse, ref_lse, rtol=0, atol=1e-6)

Hi @zyongye, I've been working on #61383 too, and part of my change overlaps with yours. I opened #65176 as a draft to share it.

Like this PR, it carries the log-sum-exp as a (max, correction) pair and computes (x - max) - correction. That part overlaps with your (hi, lo) approach, so there's no need to duplicate it. It also does two things that #61383's failing state still needs.

**Per-block sumexp without the max's 1:**
I noticed that the latest commit subtracts the max token's contribution of 1 during the global merge. However, when the max and runner-up share an 8,192-token block, `1 + exp(-18)` already rounds to `1.0` in the per-block stats pass, so subtracting 1 during the merge cannot recover the lost correction.

In #65176, the stats kernel instead excludes one max element from each block's sum to avoid this precision loss. In #61383, this issue occurs on the draft side, where `q(") ≈ 1 - exp(-gap)` and there's no op-provided log-sum-exp.

**expm1 residual:** 
_resample_kernel computes log_p + log(-expm1(log_q - log_p)) instead of log1p(-exp(delta)). With delta ≈ -1.5e-8, exp(delta) rounds to exactly 1.0, so the residual is empty even when both log-sum-exps are exact.
On a reconstruction of the issue's state (real XGrammar + Qwen3-4B tokenizer, top-k/top-p, a draft that isn't grammar-masked), main and #64242 both still emit token 0 at gap ≥ 18.

I also ran the test on this branch (ae6817425a, RTX 2050), with the test added unchanged to test_rejection_sampler_utils.py. Gaps 10 and 14 pass, but gap 25 fails under both standard and block verification: assert [1, 2, 0] == [1, 2, 3], i.e. it still resamples token 0. The other 134 tests in that file pass.

If #65103 lands first, I'm happy to rebase #65176 onto it as a follow-up with just the per-block sumexp, the expm1 residual and the test. If you'd rather fold those into your stack instead, that works for me too.

Thanks @shiannn13, you're right on both counts. The `(hi, lo)` combine here only dropped the max's 1 after each 8,192-token block had already rounded `1 + e^-gap` to 1, and the residual still went through `exp(log_q - log_p)`.

I folded both fixes and your test into this PR as e7251a11e3, with you as co-author (`Co-authored-by: Andy Shih <shiannn@icloud.com>`). Two changes from #65176:

- **Ties counted instead of an index.** The block sum leaves out one max element by counting the max's ties (`sum over x != max` plus `ties - 1`), not by taking its index. On GB300 the per-block argmax cost +20% of the verification step (K = 3, 256 requests). The tie count costs +4%, and +2–4% elsewhere.
- **Series instead of `expm1`.** The residual uses the file's existing `1 - exp(x)` series near 0 instead of libdevice `expm1`. That removes libdevice from the resample kernel and is slightly faster.

`test_resample_stays_in_target_support` is unchanged. On the previous head (78b066a8c1) it fails at gap 25 for both standard and block verification (`[1, 2, 0] == [1, 2, 3]`), as you found; it passes now along with the rest of the suite (234 passed on GB300). #64242's probe test now feeds block sums in the new convention.

Since the `(max, correction)` pair is already here, this should cover #65176 completely. Feel free to close it, or keep it open as the fallback if this stack stalls.
